title: Feature Expansion for Graph Neural Networks
summary: Graph neural networks suffer from bounded feature spaces due to linearly correlated subspaces from repeated aggregations and weight-sharing mechanisms, especially problematic when node attributes are low-dimensional. The authors propose Feature Expanded Graph Neural Network (FE-GNN) with two modifications: feature subspace flattening (independent reweighting) and structural principal components (truncated SVD of the adjacency matrix) to expand the feature space. Extensive experiments show FE-GNN achieves significant improvements, notably 73.33% accuracy on the heterophilic Chameleon dataset and an average 32% improvement over GCN on heterophilic graphs.

match_target.why: This is the user-specified target (Table 2, FE-GNN (C) on Chameleon) and represents the central result of the paper: superior node classification accuracy on heterophilic graphs due to the proposed feature expansion.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: bounded accuracy score on a test set smaller than 2,000 examples. Chameleon has 2,277 nodes total; with 20% test split, the test set has approximately 455 nodes, which is below the 2,000 threshold.

requirements.stmt: Implement feature subspace flattening with independent parameter matrices for each feature subspace
requirements.quote: we encourage each feature subspace to be independently expressed of each other in the model and weight them separately.

requirements.stmt: Construct structural principal components S via truncated SVD of the normalized adjacency matrix
requirements.quote: we extract the low-dimensional information for the graph structure to obtain its principal components: S = Q̃ Ṽ ; Â = QV^T

requirements.stmt: Combine polynomial-based feature spaces P_k(ˆL)X with structural principal components S
requirements.quote: It constructs the feature space in two ways. The first part inherits the polynomial-based GNNs and takes advantage of the multiplication of the polynomials of the structural matrix P_k(ˆL) and the node attributes X. Second, we use the principal components of the structural matrices to form another feature subspace S.

requirements.stmt: Apply column-wise normalization to ensure each column of each feature subspace contributes equally
requirements.quote: Column-wise normalization is defined as forcing ∥F·i∥2 = 1, where we take F as the concatenation of the feature space.

requirements.stmt: Use a purely linear model without activation functions or dropout, optimized with cross-entropy loss
requirements.quote: our implementation is purely linear without any deep artifices such as activation functions or dropout except for the cross-entropy loss

requirements.stmt: Use random 60%/20%/20% splits for training, validation, and test
requirements.quote: We test on the node classification task with random 60%/20%/20% splits

requirements.stmt: Report average accuracy over 100 runs with 95% confidence interval
requirements.quote: summarize the results of 100 runs in Table 2, reporting the average accuracy with a 95% confidence interval.

requirements.stmt: Use Adam optimizer with early stopping (warmup 50 epochs, patience 200, maximum 100 epochs)
requirements.quote: We employ Adam for optimization and set the early stopping criteria as a warmup of 50 pluses patience of 200 for a maximum of 100 epochs.

requirements.stmt: Use renormalized adjacency matrix Â = (D+I)^(-1/2)(A+I)(D+I)^(-1/2) with self-loops
For Chameleon, use Chebyshev polynomial (FE-GNN (C)) with order k=3 and |S|=700
requirements.quote: FE-GNN uses the Chebyshev or monomial polynomials to construct the feature space, and we refer to the corresponding versions as FE-GNN (C) and FE-GNN (M), respectively.

requirements.stmt: Set undirected graphs as assumed in the preliminaries
requirements.quote: We set these datasets to undirected graphs as we assumed in the Preliminaries.
